findings.failureScenario: source_family_id is computed with virtual_identity(), which returns "original:<uuid>" for a master photo (masterImage 0) but "master:<master uuid>" for each of its virtual copies. A master and its virtual copies therefore get different source_family_id values. The manifest's own split_policy says any later split must keep source_family_id groups intact, so a consumer that groups by this field can put the master in train and a virtual copy of the same image in test, leaking the same source pixels across splits. The field is also a byte-for-byte duplicate of virtual_copy_identity, so it adds no family grouping at all.
findings.action: Derive source_family_id from the family root, e.g. the master's uuid for both the master and its copies ("family:<root uuid>"), and keep virtual_copy_identity as the per-copy identity. Add a test with one master plus one virtual copy that asserts both rows share source_family_id.
